Physical

FIZ-ih-kuhl · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Physical is relating to the body, rather than the mind or feelings.

Climbing the rope in gym class takes a lot of physical strength.

Worked Example

Swimming is great physical exercise because it works your arms, legs, and heart.

Swimming works the body's muscles and heart, not the mind. Things about the body are physical.

How Physical Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

bodily

bodily: having to do with the body

hands-on

hands-on: done with your body, not just your mind

Antonyms

mental

mental: of the mind

emotional

emotional: of the feelings

How Strong Is It? — Active → Exhausting → physical

Active vs. physical

Active vs. physical: Active is milder: an active game gets you moving a little.

Exhausting vs. physical

Exhausting vs. physical: Exhausting is stronger: an exhausting hike uses up every bit of your energy.

The pieces

root — physic

suffix — al

suffix — al: characteristic of, relating to (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Physic- means nature and the body, so physical describes things about the body instead of the mind.
